=== axis-min-max-nullable ===
title: 'fix(type): add missing nullable type for the axis `min` and `max` option'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript users can return `null` or `undefined` from axis `min` and `max` callbacks at runtime, but the current type declarations incorrectly reject that documented pattern.

  ## Desired outcome

  The type surface for axis `min` and `max` should allow nullable callback results so the declarations match the supported API.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Axis configurations whose `min` or `max` callbacks return `null` or `undefined` pass type-checking without changing the existing runtime behavior.

  '
=== axislabel-formatter-index ===
title: 'feat(axis): axisLabel `formatter` can receive its index for working with `customValues`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Axis label callbacks can format the label value, but authors working with `customValues` also need to know which generated tick they are formatting in order to line up external labels correctly.

  ## Desired outcome

  `axisLabel.formatter` should receive the tick index as an additional argument so formatter logic can work reliably with `customValues`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A formatter declared as `axisLabel.formatter(value, index)` receives the expected index for each displayed custom tick and can build labels from that position information.

  '
=== axislabel-formatter-indexing ===
title: 'fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using custom axis label values needs labels to stay aligned with the same ordinal position they supplied, even when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent. Right now the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated values because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list instead of preserving the mapped position directly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When ECharts builds axis labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter should be called with the actual index of each rendered item in that filtered label sequence, including cases where the same numeric value appears more than once. Authors should be able to rely on formatter logic that branches on the index parameter without seeing duplicated values collapse onto the first matching position.


  ## Acceptance signals

  For duplicate or repeated custom label values that remain in range, each rendered label keeps its own formatter index and produces the text a user would expect from its own slot in the sequence. Existing axis label rendering behavior, formatter signatures, and label text generation outside this indexing bug remain unchanged.

  '
=== bar-zero-size-labels ===
title: 'fix(bar): fix wrong label position when bar width/height is 0'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Bar labels can end up on the wrong side when a bar’s width or height is zero, which is especially visible in sparse or collapsed datasets where labels matter most.

  ## Desired outcome

  Zero-size bars should still place outside labels according to the intended axis direction and inversion rules rather than falling back to a misleading default side.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars with zero width or height keep their labels on the correct visual side instead of jumping to an obviously wrong position.

  '
=== candlestick-series-encode-render ===
title: 'fix(candlestick): fix candlestick render error with `series.encode`'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Candlestick charts can render incorrectly or fail outright when data is mapped through `series.encode`, particularly in layouts that are not the simplest default case.

  ## Desired outcome

  Candlestick rendering should honor `series.encode` correctly across supported layouts so encoded dimensions still produce a valid candlestick chart.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A candlestick series driven by `series.encode` renders with the expected orientation and geometry instead of crashing or misplacing the candle bodies and whiskers.

  '
=== cartesian-small-number-rounding ===
title: Fix that extreme small numbers can not be displayed in Cartesian due to the inappropriate rounding precision.
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Extremely small numeric values can disappear or produce broken tick spacing on Cartesian charts because rounding precision removes information that still matters at the displayed scale.

  ## Desired outcome

  Axis extent and tick calculation should preserve enough precision for extremely small numbers across interval, time, and log handling so those data points remain visible.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Charts built from very small values still render meaningful extents and ticks instead of collapsing the axis or rounding the data away.

  '
=== chord-export-entry ===
title: 'fix(chord): add missing export entry for chord chart'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Developers trying to use the chord chart from the packaged library are missing the expected export entry, which makes the feature look unavailable even though the implementation exists.

  ## Desired outcome

  The published package should expose the chord chart through the expected chart entry so consumers can import and register it normally.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Using the packaged chord chart entry no longer fails because of a missing export, and the chart can be imported the same way as other supported chart types.

  '
=== datazoom-single-point-position ===
title: 'fix(dataZoom): fix wrong position of the dataZoom when the series has only one data point'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When a chart has only one data point, the slider dataZoom can compute the wrong position and render in the wrong place, which makes simple charts look broken.

  ## Desired outcome

  Slider dataZoom should place itself correctly even when the controlled series contains just a single point.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A one-point chart shows the dataZoom in the expected location instead of offsetting it because of invalid geometry calculations.

  '

  ## Desired outcome

  The public type for `nodeScaleRatio` should accept the numeric values the runtime already supports rather than implying a single fixed literal.

title: Fix/label layout margin
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors are hitting inconsistent label spacing and overlap behavior across pie charts and shared label layout code, especially around margins, stroke-aware bounds, and post-layout updates.

  ## Desired outcome

  Label layout should apply the same geometry rules everywhere so `minMargin`, `textMargin`, hidden-overlap handling, and final label bounds behave consistently after layout adjustments.

  ## Acceptance signals

category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pie labels can keep a stale curved guide line after `labelLine.smooth` is turned off or reset to zero, so option updates do not faithfully reflect the current configuration.

  ## Desired outcome

  Changing `labelLine.smooth` back to `false` or `0` should fully reset the guide line to a straight path instead of preserving the previous smoothing.

  ## Acceptance signals

  After updating `labelLine.smooth`, the rendered label line immediately matches the new setting and does not retain an old smooth curve.

  '
=== line-areastyle-empty-dimension ===

category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Line series with `areaStyle` can throw a render error when a dataset uses an empty string as a dimension name, even though that data shape should still be renderable.

  ## Desired outcome

  Area rendering should tolerate empty-string dimension names instead of treating them as a fatal path through the line-series logic.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A line chart with `areaStyle` and a dataset dimension named `''''` renders normally instead of failing during area generation.

  Animated symbols on one-way looping `lines` series can briefly flip direction when they cross the loop endpoint, which makes the motion look glitchy even though the route itself is correct.

  ## Desired outcome

  When `roundTrip` is not enabled, the effect symbol should preserve a consistent forward orientation across the loop boundary instead of flipping at the turnaround point.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A unidirectional looping line animation remains visually continuous, with the effect symbol keeping the expected orientation as it passes the loop end.

  '

category: feature

  ## Acceptance signals

  When a marker is given an explicit `z`, it renders above or below neighboring content in the same predictable way users expect from other chart elements.

  A matrix configured only with dimension lengths produces the expected headless grid structure, while existing array-based matrix definitions continue to work.

category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Matrix users can declare label formatters, but those formatters are not actually being applied, which makes matrix labels ignore both template strings and callback-based formatting logic.

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix labels should honor `label.formatter` consistently, including string templates and function formatters, and formatter callbacks should receive the expected matrix label context such as `name`, `value`, and `coord`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A matrix label configured with either formatter style renders the formatted text rather than the raw value, and callback formatters receive the documented data they need.

  '
=== parallel-axis-extent ===
title: 'fix(parallel): fix incorrect axis extent when any subsequent series has a larger value than the first'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Parallel coordinates can compute the axis extent from the first contributing series and fail to expand it for later series with larger values, causing valid data to be clipped or mis-scaled.

  ## Desired outcome

  Parallel-axis extent calculation should account for all contributing series before finalizing the displayed range.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When later series contain values outside the first series’ bounds, the parallel axis expands correctly instead of truncating the data.

  '
=== pie-tangential-noflip ===
title: 'feat(pie): add `tangential-noflip` rotation mode to keep labels tangential without flipping'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Pie labels can follow the tangent of the slice, but the current tangential mode may flip labels upside down, which is undesirable for designs that prioritize stable reading orientation.

  ## Desired outcome

  Add a `label.rotate` mode named `tangential-noflip` so tangential pie labels stay aligned to the slice without flipping to the opposite reading direction.

  ## Acceptance signals

  With `label.rotate: ''tangential-noflip''`, tangential labels remain readable and tangential while avoiding the automatic upside-down flip.

  '
=== radar-blur-itemstyle ===
title: 'fix(radar): itemStyle of blur not working'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Radar chart authors can configure blur-state styling, but `blur.itemStyle` is not actually taking effect, so blurred points keep the normal appearance instead of visually receding.

  ## Desired outcome

  Blur styling on radar series should honor the same state-specific style contract users expect elsewhere, including `blur.itemStyle` and the related line and area styling, so de-emphasized series look distinctly blurred.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When a radar series enters blur state, its symbols and associated styling follow the configured blur options instead of reusing the normal-state visuals.

  '
=== radar-clockwise-option ===
title: 'feat(radar): add `clockwise` option'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Radar charts currently assume a single indicator ordering direction, which makes it awkward to match designs or domain conventions that expect the indicators to progress clockwise.

  ## Desired outcome

  Radar coordinate systems should support a `clockwise` option so authors can choose the direction in which indicators are laid out.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Setting `radar.clockwise` changes the indicator ordering direction without breaking label placement or the rest of the radar rendering contract.

  '
=== radar-style-precedence ===
title: 'fix(radar): improve logic and add test cases of #21081'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  After the earlier radar blur fix, state-specific radar styling can still be overridden in some interaction paths, so `emphasis.itemStyle` and blur-state styling do not always win when they should.

  ## Desired outcome

  Radar state transitions should preserve the intended style precedence so emphasis and blur visuals are applied consistently instead of being overwritten by default symbol styling.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Interacting with a radar series shows the configured emphasis and blur appearance reliably, with no cases where the point styling snaps back to an unexpected default.

title: 'fix(tooltip): fix potential memory leakage by explicitly unbinding event listeners'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Applications that repeatedly create and dispose tooltip-heavy charts can accumulate leftover DOM listeners, which is the kind of slow memory growth that operators only notice after long sessions or repeated route changes.

  ## Desired outcome

  Disposing or rebuilding chart tooltips should fully release the HTML tooltip event wiring so long-lived pages do not retain stale listeners or detached tooltip state.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Repeated chart teardown and recreation no longer leaves tooltip listeners behind, and tooltip behavior remains correct without introducing leaks over time.

  '

title: 'fix(types): remove export assignment to support typescript esm compatibility'
category: bugfix

  ## Desired outcome

  The published package should expose type entrypoints that work cleanly for modern TypeScript module resolution, including distinct ESM and CommonJS declaration paths where needed.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Projects using current TypeScript ESM rules can resolve the package’s declarations without manual hacks, and mixed consumers still receive the correct type surface for their module mode.

  '

title: 'fix(type): fix missing or missmatched TS export types'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript consumers are running into missing or mismatched exported option types, especially for series that combine shared coordinate-system mixins, which makes valid configurations look unsupported in editor tooling.

  ## Desired outcome

  The published TypeScript surface should export the correct option types for affected series and include the calendar and matrix mixins where those series actually support them.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Developers importing the affected series option types no longer see missing exports or incomplete coordinate-system support in TypeScript, and valid options type-check as expected.

  '
=== visualmap-darkmode-inrange ===
title: 'fix(visualMap): fix dark mode should not provide inRange'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In dark mode, visualMap is still injecting default `inRange` colors, which can unexpectedly override the palette choices chart authors already configured for their own mappings.

  ## Desired outcome

  The dark theme should stop supplying a default `visualMap.inRange` color mapping so dark mode does not silently change how user-defined visual mapping behaves.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Enabling dark mode no longer adds an unwanted in-range color ramp, and visualMap styling follows the user’s own configuration unless they explicitly opt in to theme values.

  '
=== visualmap-unbounded-range ===
title: VisualMap support unboundedRange
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Continuous visual maps currently force both ends of `range` to behave as hard bounds, which makes it awkward to express common selections like “everything above this threshold” or “everything below this threshold.”

  ## Desired outcome

  Users should be able to mark one side of the selected interval as open-ended by enabling `visualMap.unboundedRange`, so the visual map can naturally represent one-sided ranges without custom workarounds.

  ## Acceptance signals

  With `visualMap.unboundedRange`, a range that touches the configured minimum or maximum behaves as an open interval on that side, while the opposite bound remains effective.

  '
=== vue-raw-instance ===
title: 'fix(core): mark echarts instance object as raw in Vue'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Vue users often store the chart instance inside `ref()` or `reactive()`, but proxying the ECharts instance can interfere with instance methods and create hard-to-debug integration issues.

  ## Desired outcome

  An ECharts instance should be treated as raw when used from Vue so framework reactivity does not wrap it and break normal instance behavior.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Storing the chart instance inside Vue state no longer causes proxy-related surprises, and methods like updating options or dispatching actions keep working normally.

  '
